correctness.rationale: The definition is normalized exactly by the factor 13 for (2,3). For every active support pair, a Q(sqrt(2)) positive-semidefinite certificate bounds the product by C0(N(x)^2+N(y)^2); dihedral symmetry reduces the 64 ordered support pairs to five relative classes. The standalone checker verifies all 75 principal minors exactly. A separately verified explicit pair attains the same bound, so the supremum equals the stated radical value.

originality.rationale: The defining 2021 article isolates the parameter pair (2,3) but evaluates it exactly only at the square endpoint. Full-text inspection of the 2025 p/skew generalization confirms that p=2 is the identical constant and that its concrete exact examples do not include the regular octagon. The 2024 same-object paper computes the related sum-of-squares Euler--Lagrange constants, not the product constant. Targeted published-results searches found no equivalent or stronger regular-octagon statement.

value.rationale: The parameter pair (2,3) is mathematically motivated by the defining paper itself, which uses it as its concrete two-parameter example. The regular octagon is a canonical non-Hilbert, uniformly non-square benchmark repeatedly used for exact geometric constants. Determining this exact product constant fills a natural gap between the defining endpoint calculation and the later exact sum-of-squares octagon theory; the support-certificate method also gives a reusable way to attack product-type constants on polyhedral norms.
